claims.claim: Reviewers report that high-end PC specifications or powerful hardware are required to run the game's graphics well.

citations.review_text: a great game for killing time, but high pc specs required to run on better graphics

Bought it to benchmark my PC, stayed for the breathtaking views."

If you want a game that will push your graphics card to its absolute limits and show you what modern gaming looks like, this is it.

Night City is an absolute visual masterpiece. The lighting, the path tracing, and the sheer level of detail in every neon-lit alleyway are unmatched. It is easily one of the best-looking games ever made.

Beyond the jaw-dropping graphics, the game runs incredibly well now after all the patches, and the gameplay is fast and satisfying. It’s the ultimate flex for a high-end PC.

Visuals: 11/10
Performance: Solid (post-2.0 patches)
Highly recommended if you want to melt your GPU in the best way possible.
One of the best games on PC I've ever played! Fair warning though, make sure you have a decent PC that can run the graphics on this game, would not recommend a laptop, it's worth it!

I bought the game off sale when it was 20$ and I have to say that the game is currently amazing. Everything from the graphics, to the storyline, to the attention of detail in the specific lines of each character is some of the best that I have seen in any game. However I do have one tiny complaint, while its been multiple years since the game released, I still encounter multiple bugs. None of them were major to where the game crashed, but it was annoying enough to be noticable. I would personally not buy the game at the 60$ pricetag, just wait till its on sale. Also, you would need a beefy PC to play this. 

Overall: 9/10

Turns out the world is very detailed, graphics are amazing and runs very well on my Laptop that's a bit under the recommended specs, and everything makes sense or is mostly intuitive. Basically, love it.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as well optimized and able to run smoothly across a wide variety of hardware configurations.

citations.review_text:
I anticipated, played, and repeatedly completed  Cyberpunk 2077 at release (via GOG). I even took two weeks off work to fully take in the experience on PC, using my then brand-new RTX 2060 Super. It was certainly an experience, but a mixed one. The game had various bugs and glitches and wasn't stable at all. With a little humor, I was still able to have a great time and ignore most of the technical issues.

Almost 6 years later, I gave it another try and HOLY MOLY it's a completely different game. It has fully reached the potential people saw back then. Even more than that, the developers turned it into a masterpiece.

The game can run on a wide variety of systems thanks to its highly customizable graphics settings. I tried out every setting to make it run as smoothly as possible on my build. That experience alone was fun as heck. I truly understand why this game is one of the great benchmark titles for PC hardware. It looks absolutely stunning, especially considering its age. There isn't much more that needs to be said about the graphics and performance.

The skill system seems to have been massively overhauled. Combined with your cyberware, the game now lets you create genuinely distinct builds with depth. I chose to play as a gunslinging cowboy, focused on ridiculous headshot damage and a high cool attribute. There are also many dialogue options tied to your attributes. Having certain attributes at a high level unlocks a surprising number of unique dialoge options, encouraging multiple playthroughs. In some way, this has always reminded me of Fallout NV, which is a huge compliment. I also see great potential in a Netrunner build for my next playthrough.

The story and the overall pacing are peak. I love how naturally the relationships between V, Johnny and all the other main characters develop. Keanu is a real gem and the star of the game. The choices you make genuinely matter. The world feels believable and immersive enough to lose yourself in for hours.…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat and gameplay as allowing for multiple approaches such as stealth, hacking, or direct gunplay.

citations.review_text:
As someone who started playing way after the initial launch mess, the current game is very complete and runs at least decently (if your computer meets the specifications, at least). 

Night City is probably one of the best environments and world you can make in a game. They really went the extra mile to make it immersive. 

The gameplay is above decent, you can either do slow paced hacking or fast paced bullet shooter based on how you like to play. Personally I love the netrunning and gaslighting the heck out of enemies, but it does get old fast since you just take the same approach to every mission of finding a way into their network and marking all the enemies then dealing with them sneakily.

My tip? Don't rush the main mission, there's no reason to. There's a ton of side content to explore. Don't drive around, just walk around and you'll find plenty of things to do even in the starting area.

Story wise? Meh. 

If you like being in another world with its own consistent rules, this is the game for you.

[h1] Cyberpunk 2077 is a gem everyone should try. [/h1]

I'm going to preface this review by saying yes, it had a very rough launch. But it has had massive overhauls and the game feels how it was meant to on release. The bugs are now little to none.

[b]Night City is a masterpiece of art.[/b] Driving through the neon streets is an experience I have not felt in any other experience of media. It truly feels alive, with so many people, side jobs, gigs, NCPD scans you can do, there is so much content to experience.

The 2.0 update and cyberware changes solidified the combat as [b]satisfying[/b] and [b]rewarding[/b]. You can tailor it to how you wish to play, whether you wish to be a net-runner, a cyber-samurai or go in guns blazing, the game allows you to. For most (~90%) of missions in the game you can pick how you want to play and will not need to worry about being stealthy or having to go in loud if you don't want to. The combat is a blast to play.

[b]The story is gut wrenching.[/b] The characters, especially those like Johnny feel very real. It's a gripping story that will take you through the difficult journey of V's life as to how they became what they are. There are many ending choices for this game, and many of them are very good and provide a very satisfying ending for V's story. [spoiler] Not the suicide ending, that one sucks [/spoiler] 

[h1] Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty [/h1]

The DLC adds a large amount of new story content for you to play, also fun new gigs and missions. Going through the journey with Reed and Songbird is a new experience every new and old cyberpunk fan should experience. 

After the significant changes, updates and the Phantom Liberty expansion, Cyberpunk 2077 has turned into a polished and immersive story driven experience within a well designed Night City. [b]You should play this game.[/b]

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the open world map features an abundance of marked side activities such as gigs and NCPD scanner hustles.

citations.review_text: The way the game gets you so attached to each person you met and form a connection with is insane. Even the rockerboy that lives inside your head. I smiled, laughed and cried with each character and my intercations with them. It's like you're truly living V's life. To me, that's what makes a game worth remembering and replaying. Cyberpunk is up there with Baldur's Gate 3 for me cause of that. The gameplay itself is also very enjoyable! I spent most my time running around Night City and Dogtown doing side quests, gigs, NCPD Scanner hustles, etc and forgetting that I probably should do that main questline at some point. Of course, the game has flaws just like every game tends to have but I think the pros outweigh the cons for this game. Cyberpunk 2077 and it's DLC is worth giving a try if it interests you!

The negative review is for this: Do not buy it at full price, especially not if you have a mid-range PC like mine AND especially if you are a completionist like me. I tried to experience all the content the game had to offer in a single playthrough, which led to me "optimizing" it (meaning completing all side jobs, fixer gigs and NCPD scanners). Here is my extensive review:

Six years after its original release, I thought the game would be in a pretty great state, but it is still pretty disappointing. I think most people who praise it, they do so because they compare it to the dumpster fire it was on release. But the game still feels unpolished, even unfinished, and it's still riddled with bugs. Not game-breaking ones, but they are still there. I had to install numerous mods in order to get to a decent playable state (fix for junky melee combat, pedestrian behaviour, quality of life elements for HUD and menus, like filters etc, de-scaled skill checks which were impossible after leveling up)

Gameplay wise, the RPG elements are minimal, the dialogue options are mostly different flavours of the same choice, the combat is repetitive and the enemy AI is extremely stupid, even in Very Hard difficulty. The side content (gigs and NCPD scanner jobs) are all duplicate brain-dead quests (read flavour text, go to location, sneak/shoot, loot chest, read flavour text). And no, the city is not immersive at all for me. All the places feel the same.

Its only redeeming quality, the story and characters, are overshadowed and diluted by the immense amount of mediocre side content that continuously distracts you (text messages, calls, etc) and forces you to engage with it ("wait for a whole day until the next mission objective", "find something else to do until [character] contacts you"). 

As always, I think the level design would have benefited if was a more linear and condensed experience, allowing the player to progress through the map gradually and learning to organically travers…

Shallow. Loads of variety, but it's all the same. Speccing into pistols is different from speccing into shotguns, but there's no fundamental difference between the two when the endgoal is running up and shooting someone in the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ face. Netrunner plays different, but I never leaned much into that throughout playthroughs because I find it incredibly boring. 

The same can be said about Night City itself. There's a lot of stuff to do, but it's all the same. Hundreds of NCPD alerts, but all of them can be completed right out of the tutorial, never forcing a challenge. The gigs can be somewhat more difficult, especially if you try going with the special stipulation that is always just "do it stealth lol", but both of these are all the same ♥♥♥♥ anyways: Go to a place, kill everyone, get money. I'd find that a bit more tolerable if this was unmarked, discoverable side content to supplement harder, primary side content, but no. Everything is marked on your map, free for consumption! No need to think, to observe your hollow surroundings for activities! Go where the game tells you to find Content!

Story is fine, but forced. V is whisked around by the plot to be the center of attention but never the core, only a vessel for every other character's development to revolve around. Don't worry though, you can be their muscle! And sometimes V gets monologued at by Johnny, that counts as character development too, right??

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the narrative and expansion story as standout elements of the experience.

citations.review_text:
10/10 for the Story, Phantom Liberty Story 11/10. Avoid Internet Spoilers, its worth it.

Would Play again, still playing again.

As for the Skilltree, i only used it to get the minimum Points to gain Access into Doors i needed to open.

Cyberpunk 2077 is an ok game overall that ended up having one of the most remarkable turnaround stories in modern gaming history.

The developers at CD Projekt Red put in massive work over the years to fix, finish, and overhaul what they originally started. Major updates revamped the skill trees, police systems, and combat mechanics to get the game into a genuinely complete state. While an occasional minor bug or glitch still pops up every now and then, it stays well within an acceptable range and no longer ruins the experience.

When it comes to the narrative, the main campaign has solid moments, but the Phantom Liberty expansion easily steals the spotlight. Its tighter spy-thriller story delivers far stronger pacing, sharper writing, and higher tension than the original main questline.

citations.review_text:
SCORE: 9/10

It's true this game's launch was awful. But at the time of writing this, the game is absolutely incredible. If you even find the setting of the game mildly interesting, you should give it a try. The level of polish between now and when the game launched is night and day. 

The roleplay elements are super extensive and the variety you can have in the story and the gameplay is massive between the huge amount of dialogue, guns, cyberware, eta. Not to mention the DLC is also amazing with the new ending options and the characters and their choices are incredibly compelling. 

The game is still not perfect, I did run into some bugs during my most recent playthrough however non of them were game-breaking like they were at launch. Performance is also a hitch for low to medium end PCs, I would suggest getting used to DLSS and frame gen if you are on an RTX card although I can't speak for AMD users. I will also say that CDPRs take on a FPS is a little clunky at times and can be quite noticeable when doing stuff like sliding. And finally this is an RPG at heart so if you don't like large amounts of straight up just talking and picking dialogue choices you may find yourself bored or frustrated sometimes. 

However as a person who mostly plays FPS, the content of the story was sufficient to keep me from being bored, especially as someone who really likes the setting and genre of Cyberpunk. So if you like that too you should give it a try.

Everything it's hyped to be, easily one of the best RPGs of the last decade. Only real downside is that it can be hard to run on older or weaker hardware, especially on higher resolution, I found the GTX 1070 in my old rig to be enough for 1080P 45 FPS, but anyone I know who tried with older/weaker hardware who tried had a bad time. Currently running it on a RTX 3070 (Laptop) GPU, and with upscaling It can reliably hit 60-70 FPS (I cap at 70) on the built in 2560x1600 monitor without any noticeable upscaling artifacts. Without upscaling I can hit 45 fps at the same resolution, which I find acceptable, but some people may not, especially if you're acclimated to high FPS 4k gaming.
